newsitem.title: USA: ADM to pay fines by January 14, 1997.
newsitem.headline: ADM to pay fines by January 14, 1997.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co, which has pleaded guilty to two counts of price-fixing in an ongoing U.S. Justice Department investigation, agreed Tuesday to pay $100 million in fines by January 14, 1997.
The date for the payment of the fines was approved in a federal court hearing here on ADM's plea agreement.

As reported earlier, ADM has agreed to pay a $70 million fine in the price-fixing case involving lysine, a feed additive, and a $30 million fine for citric acid, an additive used in foods, beverages and other products.
ADM was represented in the court hearing by Steven Mills, company controller, who had been appointed by a special committee of the board of directors.
Mills entered guilty pleas to the two price-fixing charges on behalf of ADM, but said he had no personal knowledge of these activities.
In the court hearing, Judge Ruben Castillo asked Mills if the board's special committee, consisting of independent directors, acknowledged that price-fixing did occur. "Yes," Mills replied.
